The National Association of Nigerian Students has passed a vote of confidence in President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, following an inspection of federal road projects in Cross River State and along the Benue-Cross River axis. The students’ body announced the decision on Saturday after completing an inspection tour to assess the quality and progress of the ongoing projects. The delegation, led by the President of the NANS Senate, Senator Ibeabuchi Onyia, comprised national officers, zonal leaders, state executives and campus leaders. The roads inspected included the Alesi-Ugep (Iyamoyung-Ugep) section in Cross River State, Sections 3A and 3B of the Calabar Coastal Highway, covering Chainage 0+000 to Chainage 65+000, and the Adikpo-Ajio-Teshe-Ada-Kyogen-Obudu Road linking Benue and Cross River states. Onyia said the delegation found the projects to be progressing to a commendable standard, adding that the site crews demonstrated discipline and technical competence. Onyia also commended the Federal Ministry of Works for what he described as its commitment to quality and professionalism in executing the projects. Speaking on behalf of Nigerian students, he declared a vote of confidence in Umahi, citing his hands-on leadership and the progress recorded on the inspected projects. He also endorsed Tinubu, praising the President’s commitment to rebuilding the country’s infrastructure and opening up regions to trade, investment, tourism and economic growth. “With this, we reaffirm our endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for his commitment to rebuilding the country’s infrastructure and opening up regions to trade, investment, tourism and economic growth,” Onyia added.
